questions.question_text: The test marks $15$, $22$, $18$ and $x$ have a mean of $19$. What is the value of $x$?

options.why: Assumed the missing mark must equal the mean instead of solving the equation.
Used $n = 3$, the number of known marks, instead of $n = 4$ when finding the total.
Gave the total of the four marks instead of subtracting the three known marks.

questions.question_text: The mean of $12$ test marks is $7.5$. What is the sum of the marks?

options.why: Added the mean to the number of marks instead of multiplying them.
Divided the number of marks by the mean instead of multiplying the mean by $n$.
Divided the mean by the number of marks instead of multiplying.

questions.question_text: The marks in a test total $1080$ and the mean mark is $45$. How many students sat the test?

options.why: Gave the mean mark again instead of the number of students.
Subtracted the mean from the total instead of dividing the total by the mean.
Multiplied the total by the mean instead of dividing the total by the mean.

questions.question_text: After $4$ tests Maya's mean mark is $66$. What must she score in her fifth test so that her mean across all five tests is $70$?

options.why: Assumed she simply needs to score the target mean in the next test.
Added the difference of $4$ to the target mean instead of comparing the two totals.
Used $n = 4$ rather than $n = 5$ for the new mean, giving $4 \times 70 - 264$.

questions.question_text: Eight students sit a test and their mean mark is $22$. Five of those students have a mean mark of $25$. What is the mean mark of the other three students?

options.why: Gave the total of the three remaining marks instead of dividing it by $3$.
Averaged the two given means instead of working with the totals of each group.
Subtracted the two given means ($25 - 22$) instead of subtracting the totals.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total of all eight} = 8 \times 22 = 176$
$\text{Total of the five} = 5 \times 25 = 125$
$\text{Total of the other three} = 176 - 125 = 51$
$\overline{x} = \frac{51}{3}$
$= 17$

questions.question_text: The mean mark for a class of $25$ students is $60$. When the results of $5$ students are excluded, the mean of the remaining $20$ rises to $64$. What is the mean mark of the $5$ excluded students?

options.why: Gave the total of the five excluded marks instead of dividing it by $5$.
Subtracted the rise of $4$ from the class mean instead of comparing the two totals.
Subtracted the two given means ($64 - 60$) instead of subtracting the totals.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total of all } 25 = 25 \times 60 = 1500$
$\text{Total of the } 20 = 20 \times 64 = 1280$
$\text{Total of the five excluded} = 1500 - 1280 = 220$
$\overline{x} = \frac{220}{5}$
$= 44$

questions.question_text: A class of $25$ students has a mean test mark of $58$. One paper was marked $47$ when it should have been marked $72$. What is the correct mean mark?

options.why: Reversed the correction, subtracting $72$ and adding $47$ to the recorded total.
Assumed a change to a single mark cannot change the mean of the class.
Added the whole $25$-mark increase to the mean instead of to the total.

questions.question_text: After $3$ tests Sam's mean mark is $62$. He has $2$ tests left, each marked out of $100$. What is the lowest mean he could have across all $5$ tests, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Divided the current total by $4$ instead of by the $5$ tests in the finished set.
Halved the current mean instead of spreading the current total over five tests.
Assumed two marks of zero would leave the mean unchanged.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total so far} = 3 \times 62 = 186$
The lowest possible is $0$ in each of the two remaining tests.
$\overline{x} = \frac{186 + 0 + 0}{5}$
$= \frac{186}{5}$
$= 37.2$
